answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity expensive to fake: require each identity to lock a scarce stake - tokens plus a long reputation history - before it can enter the river of commerce. Newcomers start in a quarantine haven where they may only transact in small amounts under peer review, with full rights unlocking gradually as their record grows. Since one operator cannot push every fake identity to the zenith of trust without paying the full staking cost each time, mass-produced sock puppets stay economically irrational.
